title: Sacred hadith
hook: words from Allah in the Prophet's phrasing, not part of the Qur'an
tomorrow: I am as My servant thinks

segments.voice: Yesterday, the four books of the Shia, and your line: four books. Did the question you named get some real thought? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-seven.

O My servants. A report in Sahih Muslim opens with those words, and the voice speaking isn't the Prophet's own. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is relating what Allah said: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. It isn't a verse of the Qur'an. You won't find it in any surah. And yet the one speaking, in the first person, is Allah. So what kind of text is this? Today's word: hadith qudsi.
screen: `O MY SERVANTS.` → `NOT A VERSE OF THE QUR'AN.` → `SO WHAT IS IT?`

segments.voice: First, the name. Hadith, a report. Qudsi, holy. So: a sacred report, one in which the Prophet relates words from Allah. Second, the layers. Listen to how these reports are built. The Prophet said that Allah said. One voice carried inside another, like a letter read aloud by the person who received it. That's today's line: allah said, he said. Third, how it differs from the Qur'an. Scholars explain it this way. The Qur'an is Allah's word in its meaning and its wording, recited in prayer, its very sound counted as revelation. A hadith qudsi carries meaning from Allah, in the Prophet's own phrasing. It isn't recited as Qur'an in the prayer. And it's graded like any other hadith, by its chain, so some are sound and some are weak. Everything from the last two weeks still applies. Fourth, the tone. Listen to this one and something stands out: it comes close. The report from Muslim keeps going. O My servants, all of you are hungry except the one I feed, so ask Me for food and I will feed you. All of you are unclothed except the one I clothe, so ask Me for clothing. And near its end: if every one of you, first and last, asked, and each were given what they asked, it would take from what Allah has no more than a needle takes from the sea when it's dipped in and lifted out. A voice that speaks of hunger, clothes, mistakes and asking. Not distant at all.
screen: `QUDSI: HOLY, SACRED.` · `THE PROPHET SAID THAT ALLAH SAID.` · `MEANING FROM ALLAH, THE PROPHET'S WORDS.` · `A NEEDLE DIPPED IN THE SEA.`

segments.voice: The practice: read one hadith qudsi, slowly, a line at a time. Settle, and breathe. First line: I have forbidden injustice for Myself. Breathe. Second: and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. Breathe. Third: ask Me for food, and I will feed you. Breathe. Fourth: a needle, dipped in the sea. Let that picture sit. Then think of today. Is there someone you might wrong without meaning to, by a word, a delay, a shortcut? Just see their face. If you pray, you can carry the line about asking into your next prayer. The bell holds the time.
Hadith qudsi. A sacred report: words from Allah that the Prophet relates in his own phrasing, outside the Qur'an. Today's word.
Your line: allah said, he said. Today, when you hear a saying passed along, ask who is speaking, and through whom. Tomorrow: I am as My servant thinks. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims read hadith qudsi for reflection and teaching, and some books gather them in one place; they are not recited as Qur'an in the ritual prayer.

notes: Muslim 2577 (Abu Dharr: 'O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself...'): confirm number; all lines paraphrased, including the needle-in-the-sea image.
'Qudsi' from the root q-d-s, shared with al-Quds (Jerusalem): standard; confirm.

The distinction (Qur'an = wording and meaning from Allah, recited in prayer, inimitable; hadith qudsi = meaning from Allah, wording of the Prophet) is the common scholarly explanation; some scholars held the wording too is from Allah. Presented as 'scholars explain it this way'; a Keeper may want the minority view noted.
